missing_spec_content.spec_text: Students should be able to explain ways of reducing unwanted energy transfers, for example through lubrication and the use of thermal insulation.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson describes wasted and dissipated energy. It never explains how to reduce unwanted energy transfers, and it does not mention lubrication or thermal insulation.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: The higher the thermal conductivity of a material the higher the rate of energy transfer by conduction across the material.
missing_spec_content.why: Thermal conductivity is not mentioned anywhere in the lesson. Conduction appears only as a named example of heating.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Students should be able to describe how the rate of cooling of a building is affected by the thickness and thermal conductivity of its walls.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson has no content on the rate of cooling of buildings, wall thickness or wall thermal conductivity.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Required practical activity 2 (physics only): investigate the effectiveness of different materials as thermal insulators and the factors that may affect the thermal insulation properties of a material.
missing_spec_content.why: The required practical on thermal insulators is not covered or referred to.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: (HT only) Students should be able to describe ways to increase the efficiency of an intended energy transfer.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson explains how to calculate efficiency and why it is below 1. It gives no ways to increase efficiency.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Throughout this section on Energy students should be able to calculate the changes in energy involved when a system is changed by: heating; work done by forces; work done when a current flows
missing_spec_content.why: Formulas for the kinetic, gravitational potential and elastic potential stores appear only in keyTerms definitions, and no calculation using them is worked through. Nothing covers calculating energy changes caused by heating or by work done when a current flows.

factual_errors.text: Magnets are moved further apart (repelling) or together (attracting)
factual_errors.correction: This is backwards. Energy in the magnetic store increases when repelling magnets are pushed closer together, or when attracting magnets are pulled further apart. Work must be done against the magnetic force. The electrostatic row in the same table states the analogous case correctly.

factual_errors.text: It becomes so spread out that it cannot be used again.
factual_errors.correction: Dissipated energy is stored in less useful ways. It is harder to use, but it is not impossible to use. The lesson's own writeBullets say "harder to use" and its memTip says "cannot easily be recovered".

wrong_terms.text: Mechanically: by a force acting on an object
Electrically: by an electric current moving through a circuit.
wrong_terms.spec_term: work done when a current flows
